recognize_zh: 視野中央一顆小至中型淋巴球，染色質緻密、細胞質稀少淡藍，細胞核被一道深凹裂分成兩葉，無中性球顆粒，可認出雙葉淋巴球（bilobed lymphocyte）。
features: Single small-to-medium lymphocyte, slightly larger than a red cell
High N:C ratio with a scant rim of pale blue, agranular cytoplasm
Nucleus divided by a deep cleft into two closely apposed lobes
Mature, condensed clumped chromatin without visible nucleoli
Background of normochromic normocytic red cells and scattered normal platelets
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic normochromic red cells and adequate platelets. A single small-to-medium lymphocyte is present with a high N:C ratio, scant agranular pale blue cytoplasm, and a nucleus split by a deep cleft into two lobes with mature condensed chromatin and no nucleoli. No blasts or cytoplasmic granulation are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with a bilobed lymphocyte, a morphologic variant that should prompt correlation with the overall lymphocyte count and clinical context.

ddx.vs: ATLL flower cells show multilobated, petal-like nuclei with more than two lobes and are usually numerous, whereas this is an isolated cell with a simple two-lobed nucleus.
Sézary cells have cerebriform, finely grooved nuclear convolutions rather than a single deep cleft producing two smooth lobes.
Granulocytes have abundant granular cytoplasm (neutral or orange-red granules), whereas this cell has only a scant agranular rim of cytoplasm.
Follicular lymphoma cells are small cleaved cells with a narrow notch and are usually accompanied by lymphocytosis; flow cytometry for CD10+ clonal B cells separates them.
